newsitem.title: India: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
LALOO YADAV CALLS MEET TO ELECT NEW LEADER

Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav decided to hold a parallel convention of the Janata Dal party on July 5 to elect a new leader. This is likely to split the party formally. The Bihar state Janata Dal president said the convention would be held either in Patna or in New Delhi and would send its report to the Election Commission. He also said Laloo Yadav would be elected as leader of the party.
The Hindustan Times
COURT ASKS FOR FILES ON JOGINER'S TRANSFER

The Patna High Court directed the government to produce all files related to the removal of Joginder Singh as the Central Bureau of Investigations (CBI) director. The court also asked the government to give reasons why it should not be proceeded against for contempt of court. The court also asked the CBI counsel to restrain the new CBI director from transferring any of its officers investigating the animal husbandry scam case without the permission of the court.
The Economic Times
BANKS ASKED TO UP CREDIT FOR EXPORTS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) asked banks to step up credit, especially to exporters and small-scale industries. Bankers said they were unable to do so as corporates were flooded with cheaper alternatives. They were also apprehensive of the sudden fall in interest rates. The bankers said any further fall would hit their spreads.
INDIA DEMANDS HIGHER TARIFF ON FARM ITEMS

India began negotiations in Geneva to bind higher import tariff on 19 agricultural products. The items may include milk products, wheat, corn and related products. India will then have to reduce tariff on mutually acceptable products to other World Trade Organisation members as compensation. India sought these negotiations under an article of the 1994 General Agreement on Tariff and Trade.
NORWEGIAN FIRM TO HAVE MAJORITY STAKE IN SHIPYARD

The government is willing to give a majority stake to Norwegian ship builder Kvaerner AS in the Hindustan Shipyard owned by the government. The yard is likely to be renamed Kvaerner-Hindustan Shipyard. The government has now approved a finance restructuring plan for the Hindustan Shipyards. This has cleared the decks for new negotiations with Kvaerner. The negotiations will now revolve around a new equity structure for the joint venture. Kvaerner had proposed to invest $10 million in the beginning and agreed to invest more later.
Financial Express
SOVEREIGN RATING MAY FALL

The swelling oil pool deficit may adversely affect India's sovereign rating which will be reviewed soon. International rating agency Standard and Poors expressed concern over the governments' inability to control the increasing oil pool deficit which now stands at 150 billion rupees. About 100 billion rupees approved by the central government as counter-guarantees are also assessed as contingent liabilities. These two may not allow India's sovereign rating to reach investment grade. The Standard and Poors is currently negotiating with the Finance Ministry on the rating.
Business Standard
TAX BREAKS PROPOSED TO BOOST EXPORTS

A core group recommended a waiver of the ceiling on royalty payments and a tax-free regime for select items to boost exports. It also suggested a de-reservation of items earmarked exclusively for the small-scale manufacturers which have blunted export competitiveness in such items. The group asked the Commerce Ministry to prepare a list of 20 to 25 items which should be given special incentives to boost exports. It also identified automobile components, computer peripherals and hardware, electronic toys and bicycle parts as the key items among these 25.
GOLD PRICE CRASHES TO A FOUR YEAR LOW

The price of standard gold crashed to a four-year low of 4,435 rupees per 10 grams in the Bombay market. This is due to the continuous weakening of the U.S. dollar and the London gold market. In the month ending July 2, gold prices fell by 320 rupees per 10 grams from 4,755 rupees on June 2. The price of 22 carat gold fell by 300 rupees per 10 grams to touch 4,100 rupees.
The Observer
INDIA REJECTS RICH NATIONS' DEMANDS

India rejected a suggestion by the industrialised nations to seek a waiver of obligations every year from the World Trade Organisation General Council. India said countries could present a phase-out plan which once accepted by the committee on balance of payment restrictions would conform with the provisions of the General Agreement on Tariff and Trade (GATT). India said there was a clear provision in the balance of payment provisions of the 1994 GATT. Pakistan, Peru and Brazil agreed with India but delegates from the United States and the European Community disagreed.
LIQUID FUEL PRICING FREED FROM CONTROL

The government removed liquid fuel pricing for independent power producers from the administered price mechanism. Officials said liquid fuel imported by private power producers on cost basis would not be linked with the oil pool account. The fuel pricing would include landed price, customs duty, countervailing duty, port charges and service charges for handling, storing and other service functions of the oil companies and, the transportation cost from the port to the power project location.
